chapter_title: The Chapter of the Man who asks: Why [am] I sometimes at peace, and troubled at other times?
chapter_note: The chapter divides cleanly into an extended dialogue-frame question (¶1-5) and a cosmological teaching answer (¶6-11). The substrate teaching is distinctive: it maps psychic disturbance and peace to two cosmic mechanisms — (1) stellar/archontic influence via roots and birth-signs, and (2) the light/dark ratio in nourishment, including a transmigration doctrine about 'justified souls' whose 'dues have ceased' entering through food. Both mechanisms stay entirely within the cosmic system. Gardner flags the 'dues have ceased' passage as potentially Buddhist-influenced (karmic consequences). The dialogue frame is unusually elaborate — three paragraphs describing the disciple's experiential states. ¶4 introduces Manichaean institutional practices (fasting, psalms, prayer) into the question. The seam flag on ¶11 is a false positive — the paragraph recaps substrate conduit-teaching without institutional application. Negative editorial fatigue score and increasing substrate density in the second half confirm the teaching core is concentrated in ¶6-11.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening: 'Once again a disciple speaks to our enlightener: I beseech you, my master.' High dialogue_frame score (36.0). No cosmological content whatsoever.

First-person phenomenological description of the peaceful state. Part of the disciple's extended question. Terms like 'Mind,' 'soul,' 'wisdom' appear but in experiential voice, not cosmic mapping. No substrate vocabulary score. The phenomenon described is what the teaching will EXPLAIN, but the description itself is not teaching.

Extended first-person description of the troubled state. Contains a substantive mechanistic question ('Are they revealed to me, or indeed did they enter me from outside?') that the teaching will address, but the framing remains experiential and personal. No cosmological vocabulary. The question about internal vs. external origin of disturbance defines the teaching topic but does not contain cosmic mapping.

Third experiential state (carefree/joyful) described in distinctly Manichaean institutional terms: 'fasting with which I fast,' 'praying,' 'psalms,' 'prayers,' 'preaching.' Institutional score 9.09. This paragraph may be an editorial elaboration of the question — the answer addresses only two states (troubled/peaceful), not three. The institutional practices color the question with the compiler's community context.
Formulaic closing of the question: 'I beseech you, my master.' Dialogue_frame score 11.43. Transitions from question to answer.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.215⟩ The soul that assumes the body, when the Light Mind will come to it, shall be purified by the power of wisdom and obedience, and it is cleansed and made a new man. There is no trouble in (the soul), nor confusion nor disturbance.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Then the apostle speaks thus to the disciple: Well do you ask about this lesson. Behold, I will explain it to you! ... Understand this:' — formulaic attribution and pedagogical transition.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching begins. The substrate describes the soul-body relationship and the Light Mind's purifying function as a cosmic process: soul assumes body → Light Mind comes → purification → new man (no trouble). Both sides of the mapping stay cosmic. The 'new man' language could be Pauline influence in translation, but the underlying mechanism (Light Mind purifying the soul in the body) is substrate cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: However, when a disturbance will arise for him and he will be troubled, this disturbance shall go into him in [ ... ], first through his birth-signs and his difficult stars that [ ... ] they turn over him and stir him and trouble him with lust and anger and depression and grief, as he wills. Also, as he wills, the powers of heaven shall trouble him through their roots, to which he is attached.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate teaching: maps celestial mechanism → psychic disturbance. Two cosmic channels: (1) birth-signs and stars that cause lust, anger, depression, grief; (2) powers of heaven acting through their 'roots' to which the person is 'attached.' Both sides stay within the cosmic system. 'Roots' (conduits connecting celestial powers to embodied souls) is key substrate vocabulary — cf. Ch.48 on roots and conduits.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, there are times you shall find the powers of heaven are peaceful and tranquil for him, and it comes to [ ... ] a difficult part comes into him by the nourishment that he has eaten, or else indeed in some [ ... ] or in the water that they have drunk. Again, trouble and confusion and anger will increase in him, and lust multiplies upon him together with depression and grief; because of the nourishment of the bread he has eaten and the water he has drunk, which are full of bothersome parts, a vengeful counsel. They shall enter his body, [mixed in] with these foods, and they even become joined in with the wicked parts of the body and the Sin that is in him; transferring the anger and the lust and the depression and the grief, these wicked thoughts of the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate: maps nourishment mechanism → psychic disturbance. Even when celestial powers are calm, food/drink containing dark 'parts' enters the body and joins with the body's own dark element ('the Sin that is in him'). The teaching describes cosmic mixture at the level of food: bread and water as carriers of bothersome/vengeful parts that transfer to the body's faculties. 'Sin' capitalized as it functions here as the cosmic dark substance inherent in the material body — a remnant of the original light-dark mixture.

paragraphs.core_text: should you be troubled [ ... ... ] them through the conduits and the roots of they above [ ... ... ] the flood that comes into you.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Now, behold, I have explained to you that' — transitional attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose transitional paragraph. Substrate vocabulary survives in fragments: 'conduits,' 'roots of they above,' 'the flood.' These are cosmic architecture terms — conduits and roots as channels between celestial powers and embodied souls. The 'flood' entering the person describes the mechanism of cosmic influence. Despite lacunae, the substrate terminology is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: There are times, however, if you shall find that the nourishment that comes into you is pure [ ... ... ], so it is greater in light and life while the waste is less in it, and the evil-doing is diminished from it. Even the atmosphere above is still, being purified through the [ ... ... ] also the image is calmed from [ ... ... ] increases in you through ⟨p.216⟩ those good parts of the food that come into you. And they find you at ease and tranquil, as you are well governed in your abodes because of the living part, which is greater on account of the light of these justified souls that are in it. The ones that have perfected their deeds. Their dues have ceased, while their soul is carefree [ ... ] they have been allied with these living souls that [are p]resent in you. Due to this you shall find them in you, calm in tranquillity, and they come from you without trouble; and you are found flourishing of body. Even your deeds are determined, being well constructed after their manner, and your doctrines are in order, as your words [ ... ] your soul is carefree within you, ascending like a bird.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The richest substrate paragraph. Maps the positive mechanism: pure nourishment (greater in light, less waste) → peace. Introduces a transmigration doctrine: 'justified souls' whose 'dues have ceased' enter through food and ally with the living souls in the person. Gardner flags 'their dues have ceased' as potentially Buddhist-influenced (karmic consequences). 'Ascending like a bird' is a soul-correspondence. 'Abodes' likely refers to the body's cosmic chambers/faculties. 'The image is calmed' — 'image' as a cosmic term for the body's form. All mappings stay within the cosmic system: nourishment quality → light/dark ratio → transmigrated souls → alliance with inner light → psychic peace → soul ascending.

paragraphs.core_text: when [your bo]dy is troubled, you shall be troubled by the conduits of they below, the difficult parts that come into you by food and the act of eating. Again, when the conduits above are calmed from you, even your food that has come into you is clear and pure. Your heart shall be found ordered in its place, your counsels at peace from disturbance.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Behold, I have explained to you the determination of this lesson for which you asked: Whence come these bad counsels and considerations into you, these vengeful thoughts that trouble; and also whence come into you these good counsels and sweet doctrines, when your Mind is calmed for you. I have told you that' — recap attribution and question restatement. The seam flag appears to be a false positive — this paragraph recaps substrate conduit-teaching, not institutional application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary paragraph with dialogue frame wrapping substrate recap. The teaching content distills the two-mechanism model into a clean formula: (1) conduits below + bad food → trouble; (2) conduits above calmed + pure food → peace. 'Conduits of they below' and 'conduits above' are key substrate architecture terms. The binary conduit system (above/below) summarizes the teaching of ¶7-10. Despite the seam flag, no institutional vocabulary is present — this is a recapitulation of cosmic mechanism.

Narrative closure: the disciple glorifies the apostle. 'You are glorious and blessed!' — formulaic praise response. No cosmological content. Standard Q&A session ending in the Kephalaia compilation format.
